response.reasoning:
Before buying, the buyer asked specifically about box condition and was told the boxes were fine, having been stored in a cupboard since new; the listing said the same. That makes box condition part of what was promised, not an incidental detail. The photograph the buyer took of the set shows a genuinely crushed and split corner on one of the four boxes, which is not consistent with what was described. The photograph of the shipping carton shows it square, taped and with no crush or impact damage on the outside, so it is hard to attribute the crushed corner to rough handling in transit crushing the parcel; either the damage was there before the set was packed, or the set was not padded enough inside a carton that itself survived. Either way that sits on the seller's side of the line, and the delivery record shows an ordinary journey with no incident. The buyer also raised it the day it arrived, which is prompt.

Against that, this is a purchase of four sets for two hundred, and only one box is shown as damaged. Nothing suggests the contents of that set are affected, and nothing suggests the other three boxes are anything other than as described. So the shortfall is the collector's premium on one box out of four, not the value of the order. A fifth of the money being held reflects that loss fairly: the buyer keeps four sets, three of them as promised and one with a damaged box, and is compensated for the difference between the set he was promised and the one he received.

findings.statement: Before the sale the buyer asked directly whether the boxes were in good condition and said that for a retired set the box is most of what he is paying for; the seller answered that the sets had been stored in a cupboard since new and the boxes were fine.
The listing described the sets as used, like new, with boxes in good condition, at a price of 200 for four sets.
The buyer's photograph of the set shows a crushed and split corner at the top left of the box, with the rest of the box intact; this is inconsistent with the described condition.

The buyer's photograph of the shipping carton shows it square and undamaged on the outside, with intact tape and no crushing, which does not support the damage having been caused by the parcel being crushed in transit.
The delivery record shows a normal journey from handover to delivery over two days with no exception or damage event.
The buyer reported the damaged corner on the day of delivery, and the seller replied that the item was in good condition when it left and was carefully packed.
The buyer said something was wrong immediately on receiving the goods, within the time allowed under the record of the purchase.
Only one of the four boxes is shown as damaged, and nothing in the evidence suggests the contents of that set or the other three sets are affected.
